[1/3] Plan collapse/expand rows for the draggable hierarchy tree

impact_assessment.why: The hierarchy tree now renders every node, so large scenes become a long unwieldy list with no way to fold subtrees.
impact_assessment.benefits: Nodes with children get a collapse toggle, descendants hide while folded, filtered searches reveal matches, and selecting a hidden node expands its ancestors.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: UI-only, no API/schema change; dependency: none; concurrency: editor lock; state: stale collapse ids, drag/drop on collapsed rows, filter behavior, selection reveal, rebuilding rows.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep collapse state in a Set, hide only descendants of collapsed nodes, bypass collapse while filtering, reveal selected ancestors, and add static tree/collapse regressions.

[1/3] Plan an AI-readable scene validation report with missing assets, prefab links and naming warnings

impact_assessment.why: AI and human authors can save scenes with missing registry assets, dangling prefab links or duplicate names without an explicit preflight report.
impact_assessment.benefits: A validate_scene action returns structured errors/warnings with node ids and fields, and the console shows a compact validation summary before saving.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: editor schema 42 and one new action; dependency: none; concurrency: editor lock; state: registry identity checks, prefab cache gaps, duplicate-name grouping, empty groups, reset between actions.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Build the report from scene objects and registry identity, group duplicate names, keep warnings non-fatal, expose counts, and add valid/missing-asset/dangling-link/duplicate-name regressions.

[1/3] Plan editable translate/rotate/scale snap increments persisted with the workspace layout

impact_assessment.why: Snap rounding is hard-coded to 0.25 units, 15 degrees and 0.1 scale, so authors cannot match a project grid or angle convention.
impact_assessment.benefits: Three numeric controls set positive snap increments, all gizmo rounding uses them, and the values persist and reset with the workspace layout.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: UI-only, no API/schema change; dependency: none; concurrency: editor lock; state: invalid or zero increments, layout migration, reset defaults, wheel/translate/rotate/scale paths.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Validate finite positive increments, fall back to defaults, include them in layout snapshots/restoration, route every snap path through the stored values, and add static regressions.

[1/3] Plan project-relative asset import into the manifest and registry

impact_assessment.why: The editor can assign registry assets but cannot import new mesh, texture or prefab files, so authors must edit keystone.json and restart the server.
impact_assessment.benefits: An import_asset action validates a project-relative .obj/.png/.kprefab, registers project:<path>, updates the manifest atomically, and the console exposes a path input and imported-asset readout.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: editor schema 43 and one new action; dependency: project context; concurrency: editor lock; state: path traversal, unsupported/glTF formats, manifest rollback, replace semantics, registry load failures.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Require --project context, resolve and contain the path, reject unsupported/glTF formats with guidance, save the manifest atomically, roll back on register failure, and add import/idempotence/error regressions.

[1/3] Plan hot reload of file-backed assets with scene and history rebinding

impact_assessment.why: Imported and project assets are only read at import or startup, so after re-exporting an .obj/.png the editor keeps stale payloads and offers no structured reload report.
impact_assessment.benefits: reload_assets calls AssetRegistry.refresh(), rebinds scene mesh/material references plus undo/redo snapshots, and reports checked/reloaded/failed/missing/rebound counts in the console.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: editor schema 44 and one action; dependency: AssetRegistry.refresh; concurrency: editor lock; state: failed/missing files, stale history payloads, shared payload identities, prefab payloads not rebindable, unchanged files yielding new payload objects.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Capture old records before refresh, map only changed payload identities, rebind node and history references by identity, keep last-good payloads on failure, report counts, and add changed/failed/missing/no-registry/history tests.

[1/3] Plan editor glTF/GLB scene import with prefab generation and manifest tracking

impact_assessment.why: The CLI imports glTF/GLB scenes into prefab libraries, but the editor rejects them, so authors must edit keystone.json and restart to bring in a 3D scene.
impact_assessment.benefits: import_gltf imports a project-relative .gltf/.glb, generates a project prefab, registers gltf.<stem>.* assets, appends the source to keystone.json, reports prefab/assets/replaced state, and the console routes glTF paths automatically.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: editor schema 45 and one action; dependency: project context and PrefabLibrary; concurrency: editor lock; state: parse failures after manifest save, partial registry assets, prefab name collisions, duplicate reimports, external glTF buffers, stale prefab cache.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Validate path, suffix and name before saving, snapshot registry ids for added-asset cleanup, roll back the manifest on failure, pop stale prefab cache entries, rely on atomic prefab saves, and add success/reimport/error/no-project/no-library tests.
